title: On The Implications of the Unalienability of the Right of Authorship for Ghostwritting Contracts

detail.title: On The Implications of the Unalienability of the Right of Authorship for Ghostwritting Contracts
detail.abstract: This paper will argue that the right of authorship is unalienable even when it becomes subject to a commercial contract (of which some of examples are ghostwriting agreements such as those for political speeches and autobiographies). The paper will argue further that the general concept of moral rights is weakened by theories which allow ghostwriting in order to keep the theory of copyright law close to practice. Practice, however, is sometimes morally dubious. This paper’s purpose is to show that ghostwriting defies many rules as the scope of the term encompasses many.

title: Critical Peak Rewards: Evidence from a Nationwide Demand Response Program
affiliations: Centre for Net Zero, Columbia University and Centre for Net Zero

detail.title: Critical Peak Rewards: Evidence from a Nationwide Demand Response Program
detail.abstract:
Demand flexibility at scale is likely to be an important part of the future energy system. This study evaluated the world’s first nationwide domestic and commercial demand flexibility program. We analyzed the policy using a natural field experiment, with a sample of 2.7 million, assigning 119,999 customers to a control group and the rest to receive randomized encouragement to sign up to the demand flexibility program. The program paid consumers to reduce their demand below a predicted baseline at peak demand across 16 events (i.e., when the system was stressed) during the Winter of 2023–24. Customers who opted into events reduced demand during events by 23.1% among compliers, at an average cost for the system operator of £2,325 per MWh. The adoption of solar panels and batteries, heat pumps, and EVs all increased demand response.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Contractual Lock-in and the Timing of Green Transitions: Evidence from Industrial Chemical Supply in Brazil's Pulp Industry
affiliations: , Itaipu Technological Park Foundation, Itaipu Technological Park Foundation, Itaipu Technological Park Foundation, Itaipu Technological Park Foundation and Itaipu Technological Park Foundation

detail.title: Contractual Lock-in and the Timing of Green Transitions: Evidence from Industrial Chemical Supply in Brazil's Pulp Industry
detail.abstract: This study investigates the structural mechanisms that determine the technological trajectory of industrial plants with respect to the carbon intensity of chemical inputs sourced from third parties. The empirical context is the hydrogen peroxide supply market for pulp bleaching in Mato Grosso do Sul, a state that concentrates four world-class plants built at distinct points in time over approximately fifteen years. The central argument is that the moment at which each plant formalized its chemical supply contracting decision, relative to the moment at which the integrated green supply model became commercially available, determines its technological trajectory over a horizon of fifteen to twenty years. This contractual lock-in emerges from the combination of asset specificity of the supplier installed on the buyer's site, bundling of complementary products, and contractual incompleteness that renders the carbon intensity of the input a credence attribute, unverifiable by the buyer from the product received. The study offers three additional contributions with implications for climate policy. First, that observed adoption of a green input does not imply revealed preference, and may instead result from a coincidence of timing with no contractualized valuation of the environmental attribute whatsoever, what we term an accidental green transition. Second, that buyers with favorable scale and timing may deliberately adopt a partially green supply model, contractually separating the supply of ClO₂ and H₂O₂, with the latter sourced from H₂ captured from the kraft process itself, what we term fragmented green supply. Third, that green market share indicators may register apparent backsliding even without any reversal of trajectory, due to a dilution effect caused by the entry of new conventional capacity. The theoretical framework integrates transaction cost economics, path dependence, and credence attribute theory, deriving four intervention points ordered by expected cost-effectiveness.

title: Economic Models of Identity Formation and Cultural Transmission
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - Department of Economics and Paris School of Economics (PSE)

detail.title: Economic Models of Identity Formation and Cultural Transmission
detail.abstract:
In this paper we survey recent advances in the economic theory of identity formation. We restrict our analysis to models which conceptualize identity formation as embedded into an inter-generational cultural transmission process, and therefore have implications for the dynamics of social identity. Through the lens of a general framework linking identity formation to cultural evolution, we discuss issues related to the dynamics of oppositional, racial, or minority attitudes, cultural polarization, identity switching, and openness to alternative identities. An application of the set-up to multidimensional identities constructed from combinations of characteristics, provides conditions under which societies converge (or not) toward narrow identities centered on salient markers such as religion, ethnicity, or race. We conclude by outlining promising avenues for future research.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Bank Runs With and Without Bank Failure
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management

detail.title: Bank Runs With and Without Bank Failure
detail.abstract:
We study the causes and consequences of bank runs. By applying large language models to historical newspapers, we create a comprehensive database of bank runs in U.S. history with information on 3,984 runs on individual banks from 1863 to 1934. Our novel data allow us to establish that runs are considerably more likely in weak banks but also occur in strong banks, especially in response to negative news about the real economy or the broader banking system. However, runs typically only result in failure for banks with poor fundamentals. Strong banks survive runs through various mechanisms, including signaling strength, interbank cooperation, and temporary suspension. At the local level, runs on banks with poor fundamentals translate into substantially larger declines in deposits, lending, and manufacturing activity than runs on strong banks. Our findings imply that poor fundamentals are central to explaining both when runs occur and when they have severe economic effects, tempering the view that small shocks can generate discontinuous jumps to bad equilibria through self-fulfilling run dynamics.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Internal Revaluation and Disequilibrium in Balance of Payments: The Role of Interest Rates in a Stylized Analytical Model

detail.title: Internal Revaluation and Disequilibrium in Balance of Payments: The Role of Interest Rates in a Stylized Analytical Model
detail.abstract: The paper investigates interest rates adjustments as a mechanism to restore the Balance of Payments equilibrium disrupted in the first place by internal revaluation. The context of the study is an economic crisis in a country that has undergone internal revaluation thereby losing its price competitiveness and developing an unsustainable current account deficit. I show that, in equilibrium, internal revaluation implies higher (lower) interest rates as long as aggregate savings are less (more) sensitive to interest rates than imports. The finding carries over to the more realistic scenario of relative internal revaluation as well when the economy is revalued only relative to its trading partner. This suggests that the mechanism of interest rates adjustments could be effective also in those instances when internal revaluation has solely resulted from the trading partner becoming gradually "cheaper". Applying this insight into the structural imbalances of the Euro Area, that have materialized following the Great Recession of 2007-2009, demonstrates that the predominant policy of keeping interest rates artificially low in Southern Europe is, in fact, not optimal in the sense of the Balance of Payments equilibrium. Furthermore, letting interest rates rise under market forces would contribute not only to efficient pricing of risks but also to the potential elimination of external imbalances.

title: A Technical Typology of AI Systems in Public Administration
affiliations: University of Oxford - Oxford Internet Institute, Hertie School - Centre for Digital Governance, University of Oxford - Oxford Internet Institute, Hertie School of Governance, University of Oxford - Oxford Internet Institute and University of Utrecht

detail.title: A Technical Typology of AI Systems in Public Administration
detail.abstract: Research on artificial intelligence (AI) in the public sector often treats "AI" as a single category, neglecting technical distinctions between different AI systems. But these distinctions affect how different systems impact core public values like accountability, procedural justice, and non-discrimination. This paper argues that public administration research would benefit from more technical precision on "AI" and makes three contributions to this end. First, we introduce a typology of five categories of AI systems: handcoded, glass-box, black-box, general-purpose, and agentic systems. We calibrate the typology to public administration by grouping system types by their distinct implications for public values. Second, we evaluate technical precision in recent public administration research about AI by coding 91 highly-cited papers (2019-2025) using our typology. We find widespread imprecision: most papers (55%) leave the studied system underspecified, 31% motivate their work with a different system than they study, and 41% make more general conclusions than the studied system supports. Finally, we give practical recommendations for future research. We highlight common pitfalls to avoid, and suggest that researchers should, at a minimum, provide enough technical detail to locate the studied system in our typology. To this end, we provide a practical guide-a short set of diagnostic questions answerable from public information and without specialist technical knowledge.

title: Emissions Trading Schemes, Market Liquidity, and Corporate Debt Financing Costs: Evidence from China
affiliations: Jinan University and Jinan University

detail.title: Emissions Trading Schemes, Market Liquidity, and Corporate Debt Financing Costs: Evidence from China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses secondary firm-level financial data and publicly available carbon market information and does not involve human participants, patients, or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Using China's seven regional emission trading scheme (ETS) pilots (2013-2020) as a staggered quasi-natural experiment, this paper documents that the relationship between ETS participation and corporate debt financing costs is sharply conditioned on market liquidity. In high-tradingvolume markets-where institutional certification is credible-enrollment is associated with an immediate reduction in the realized debt-financing-cost ratio (financial expenses over total liabilities) of approximately 0.8-1.3 percentage points that persists through the third postenrollment year; in low-trading-volume markets, the effect is economically negligible and statistically indistinguishable from zero. Because the dependent variable is scaled by total rather than interest-bearing liabilities, these magnitudes should be read as proportional shifts in a lowbase ratio rather than as direct loan-spread changes. Mechanism analysis is most consistent withthough it does not directly identify-the lenders' pricing of ETS enrollment as an institutional certification signal rather than mediation through observable firm behavioral adjustments, drawing on a continuous liquidity-interaction design, a non-parametric split-sample event study, a pricevs.-quantity bank-lending test, and Sobel exclusion tests across six candidate firm-behavior mediators. Heterogeneity analysis confirms larger effects for non-state-owned enterprises and firms in financially underdeveloped regions, consistent with an information asymmetry framework. Consistent with this conditionality, the national ETS launched in 2021 produces no robust financing-cost effect in its inaugural year: a marginally positive triple-difference coefficient is fully absorbed by industry-and province-level time-varying controls, as predicted for a nascent, low-liquidity market. These findings reframe ETS evaluation: within the range of institutional settings we observe, market liquidity appears to be not merely a narrow efficiency criterion but a precondition for the financing co-benefits of emissions trading to materialize.

title: The Triple Identity: Kelly Growth, KL Divergence, and the Dual Bregman Cost of the Logarithmic Market Maker
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Triple Identity: Kelly Growth, KL Divergence, and the Dual Bregman Cost of the Logarithmic Market Maker

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interest that influenced this study; its results synthesize established results from the cited literature.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical and mathematical study with no human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: We record a clean identity for the logarithmic market scoring rule (LMSR), read as a market maker over the probability simplex. For a trader with belief P trading against a pool state Q with liquidity parameter b, three quantities coincide: the maximum Kelly log-growth rate G*, the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence from belief to pool D_KL(P || Q), and the dual Bregman divergence of the LMSR cost per unit liquidity, D_C*(P,Q)/b. That is, G* = D_KL(P || Q) = D_C*(P,Q)/b. The trade cost itself decomposes, by convex duality, into a primal information charge b * D_KL(pre || post) and a fair-value exposure term. This Kelly alignment is special to the logarithmic (KL) generator: the squared-Euclidean (L2) cost-function market maker has a dual Bregman divergence that is not the Kelly growth rate. Each ingredient is classical: Kelly = KL; the LMSR-Bregman correspondence (the LMSR dual Bregman = KL and the L2 Bregman appear as standard cost-function market-maker examples); convex duality. The contribution is narrow and expository, the explicit, dimensionally consistent assembly into the triple identity, with the primal-charge versus dual-extraction distinction made sharp. We claim no new theorem. This note isolates the certain results; the uniqueness and selection theorems, the equilibrium analysis, and the settlement-governance and protocol constructions are developed in companion work. It builds on the free-energy, Kelly, and KL foundations of the companion paper, The Free Energy Identity (ResearchGate and SSRN, 2026).

title: Droit Moral in Selected Legal Systems of Asia, By Example of the Right to Authorship of a Work: Where Are We Coming From, And Where Are We Going

detail.title: Droit Moral in Selected Legal Systems of Asia, By Example of the Right to Authorship of a Work: Where Are We Coming From, And Where Are We Going
detail.abstract: The specification of droit moral in Asian countries cannot be encapsulated uniformly in a clear-cut way, as the individual countries present certain dissimilarities in this respect. It is, however, possible to attempt to establish groups showing the general mechanisms governing the development of moral rights in this part of the world. A presentation of the copyright regulations of Asia gains importance if we concentrate on the currently progressing globalisation of intellectual property rights (Jena, 2005: p. 7; Swadźba, 2006: p. 33–39) and the convergence of the Asian countries’ economies (Freeman, 2003: p. 158–159). This analysis will be carried out based on the laws of countries such as: Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, the Philippines, Vietnam, India, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Japan.

title: Did Draghi's 'Whatever It Takes' Speech Compress Sovereign Spreads? Evidence from a Continuous-Treatment Event Study Difference-in-Differences

detail.title: Did Draghi's 'Whatever It Takes' Speech Compress Sovereign Spreads? Evidence from a Continuous-Treatment Event Study Difference-in-Differences
detail.abstract: This paper estimates the causal effect of Mario Draghi's 'Whatever It Takes' speech of 26 July 2012 on sovereign bond spreads across ten eurozone member states. Using a continuous-treatment event-study difference-indifferences design, I exploit crosssectional variation in 2011 debt-to-GDP ratios as a proxy for treatment intensity, with country and date fixed effects absorbing time-invariant heterogeneity and common daily shocks. The principal finding is a coefficient of-0.683 basis points per 1 percentage point increase in debt-to-GDP, significant at the 1% level. Italy experienced approximately 46 basis points more spread compression than Finland, a roughly 7 per cent reduction in borrowing costs attributable to a single verbal commitment, absent any bond purchases. Pre-period parallel trends hold (F(9, 289) = 1.55, p = 0.131), and the results are robust to alternative event windows, debt-to-GDP vintages, and the exclusion of outliers. A regression-based test for heterogeneity by programme status is inconclusive given the limited number of programme countries in the sample. These findings demonstrate that central bank credibility and expectation management, rather than the scale of intervention, are the primary transmission channels by which communication influences sovereign debt markets during crises.

title: Forecasting ZAR/USD Volatility: A Comparative Study of GARCH, Stochastic Volatility, and Machine Learning Models in an Emerging Market Context
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Forecasting ZAR/USD Volatility: A Comparative Study of GARCH, Stochastic Volatility, and Machine Learning Models in an Emerging Market Context

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Declaration of Interest: The author declares no conflicts of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available financial market data and requires no ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: Type This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Accurate volatility forecasting is central to risk management, derivatives pricing, and policy in emerging markets, yet the South African Rand (ZAR) remains under-studied despite high sensitivity to global shocks and capital flow reversals. This paper compares three modeling paradigms for ZAR/USD daily volatility from 2010 to 2025: classical GARCH/EGARCH models, latent Stochastic Volatility (SV) estimated via MCMC, and machine learning approaches including LSTM and Random Forest. Using a rolling out-of-sample design, we evaluate forecasts with MSE, QLIKE, and Diebold-Mariano tests. We find that LSTM and Random Forest models outperform GARCH during high-volatility regimes and short forecast horizons, while SV models provide more stable density forecasts during crisis periods. GARCH(1,1) remains competitive in calm regimes but suffers from estimation error in thin, structurally unstable data. The results inform risk models for South African financial institutions and the South African Reserve Bank. All code and data procedures are provided for replication at https: //github.com/henrymayambu/zar-volatility.

title: Two Problems, One Incomplete Fix: Newey-West Corrects for Overlap Autocorrelation But Not Overlap Bias, and Fat Tails Make the Uncorrected Problem Larger

detail.title: Two Problems, One Incomplete Fix: Newey-West Corrects for Overlap Autocorrelation But Not Overlap Bias, and Fat Tails Make the Uncorrected Problem Larger

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
The standard remedy for rolling-window statistics evaluated against overlapping outcome windows is to apply Newey-West HAC standard errors. This remedy is correct but incomplete. It addresses one of two distinct problems introduced by overlapping estimation and outcome windows: serial correlation inflation, which biases t-statistics upward. It does not address the second problem — directional bias in the point estimate, which biases the estimand itself in a predictable direction. These are separate problems requiring separate remedies.

We formalize this decomposition for the payoff asymmetry statistic PA = E[r | r > 0] / E[|r| | r < 0], estimated over a trailing 756-day window of daily returns evaluated against 60-day forward outcomes (overlap fraction $\varphi = 60/756 \approx 7.9\%$). Using 106,163 stock-month observations across 715 U.S. equities from 2009 to 2025, we demonstrate that: Problem 1 (serial correlation) is correctly addressed by Newey-West with $L = \lceil 60/21 \rceil = 3$ lags and effective sample size $n_{\text{eff}} \approx 28{,}240$; Problem 2 (directional bias) shifts the bottom-decile win rate by $-12.9$ percentage points and the top-decile win rate by $+3.6$ percentage points, compressing a $+11.3$pp prospective spread to a $-5.2$pp reversed spread — and is not corrected by any standard error adjustment. Under fat-tailed return distributions ($\hat{\alpha} = 2.69$, FAT class), Problem 2 is amplified beyond the O($\varphi$) first-order prediction by a factor we calibrate at $\approx 1.6\times$. The mechanism is not that fat-tailed extreme observations are larger in absolute terms than Gaussian extremes (they need not be at $\alpha = 2.69$), but that a single extreme contaminating observation contributes disproportionately to the ratio statistic relative to the typical observation: its magnitude relative to the distributional mean is larger than under Gaussian assumptions, and conditioning on a positive outcome truncates extreme losses from the denominator by an amount that grows as $\alpha$ decreases. Researchers who apply Newey-West and treat the overlap issue as resolved cannot determine from that result alone whether significance reflects genuine signal, Problem 1, or Problem 2.

title: Liquidity Constraints, Cash Windfalls, and Entrepreneurship: Evidence from Administrative Data on Lottery Winners
affiliations: National Chengchi University (NCCU) - Department of Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Chengchi University (NCCU) and Academia Sinica - Institute of Economics

detail.title: Liquidity Constraints, Cash Windfalls, and Entrepreneurship: Evidence from Administrative Data on Lottery Winners
detail.abstract: This paper examines the causal effect of financial resources on entrepreneurial decisions by exploiting wealth shocks from lottery winnings. Using administrative panel data that link lottery winners to business registration records in Taiwan, we employ a triple-differences design that leverages variation in prize size and compares current versus future lottery winners. The results show that receiving a large lottery prize exceeding 1.5 million NT$ (approximately 50,000 US$) increases the number of businesses owned by 0.025 (a 12.3% increase relative to the baseline mean), with effects that persist over at least five years. For individuals without prior business ownership, large windfalls raise the probability of entrepreneurial entry by 1.5 percentage points. This entry response is driven by individuals with high pre-winning earnings but no liquid savings and is concentrated in incorporated rather than unincorporated ventures. For existing business owners, large windfalls increase incorporated business holdings by 10.7%, but do not significantly affect the continuation of businesses owned before winning.

title: The British Tax Reform Framework: A Proposal for Continuous Personal Income Taxation and Employment-Weighted Business Taxation.

detail.title: The British Tax Reform Framework: A Proposal for Continuous Personal Income Taxation and Employment-Weighted Business Taxation.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial interests, personal relationships or competing interests that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is a conceptual policy proposal and does not involve human participants, personal data, clinical research or experiments requiring ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the British Tax Reform Framework (BTRF), a two-part tax reform model combining a continuous personal income tax schedule with an employment-weighted business tax. The first component, the Progressive Earnings Curve (PEC), replaces stepped income tax bands with a smooth mathematical function linking gross income to take-home pay. The second component, the Employment-Weighted Business Tax (EWBT), adjusts business profit taxation according to the share of business value paid to workers and the amount of full-time-equivalent employment created. The proposal is intended to improve transparency, preserve progressivity, raise additional revenue for public finances and encourage employment-intensive business activity. The paper presents the formulas, worked examples, a comparison with the current UK system, policy rationale, risks, safeguards and areas requiring further modelling.

title: Media Attention Structural Inequality: A Comparative Analysis of Parasport and Traditional Sport Coverage

detail.title: Media Attention Structural Inequality: A Comparative Analysis of Parasport and Traditional Sport Coverage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No potential conflict of interest was reported by the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved an anonymous online survey of adult participants (N=290) about media consumption habits. All participants provided informed consent. The survey did not collect any sensitive personal data. Formal ethics approval was not required as the study does not involve medical or clinical interventions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The study was conducted as an independent research project.

detail.abstract: This study presents a systematic empirical investigation of structural inequality in the media representation of adaptive (Paralympic) sport relative to conventional sport across Russia's two dominant digital sports platforms, Championat.com and Sports.ru. Employing a concurrent mixed-methods research design that integrates quantitative content analysis of website and social media output with a sociological survey instrument administered to 290 respondents, the research generates precise, triangulated measurements of the informational asymmetry between these two categories of sport coverage. Findings reveal a publication ratio of 528:0.07 (Championat.com) and 80:0 (Sports.ru) in average daily terms during non-Paralympic periods, providing full empirical confirmation of both the structural inequality hypothesis (H₁) and the audience perception hypothesis (H₂). Theoretical interpretation proceeds through the analytical frameworks of agenda-setting theory, framing theory, cultural hegemony, the social construction of reality, and Bourdieuian symbolic inequality. The study makes an original contribution to the underexplored intersection of disability media studies and Russian sports journalism scholarship, offering a replicable methodological framework and a set of evidence-based recommendations addressed to editorial boards, sports governing bodies, and relevant state authorities.

title: Efficient "Risk Attitudes"
affiliations: and University of Zurich - Laboratory for Social and Neural Systems Research

detail.title: Efficient "Risk Attitudes"
detail.abstract: Choices under risk are widely used to estimate risk preferences, probability weights, and welfare-relevant utility curvature. This paper shows that these preferences and related objects can be misidentified when lottery attributes must first be represented with finite precision. We study a Bayesian agent who maximises expected reward but must allocate a single representation invariant Fisher geometric capacity that can be normatively distributed across payoff and probability representations. The optimal noisy representation structure generates several canonical risk attitude patterns without assuming curvature in utility or nonlinear probability weighting. Imprecise payoff representation alone produces risk seeking at low stakes and risk aversion at higher stakes, even when probabilities are known exactly, with a reversal threshold that varies systematically with the success probability and the payoff environment. When probabilities are also represented imprecisely, right-skewed payoff environments endogenously allocate more precision to low probabilities and can generate apparent overweighting of rare events. The model also yields a closed-form rule for the optimal split of a common capacity budget across payoff and probability attributes, and the framework is generalizable beyond lotteries. Estimated on two large risky choice datasets, the model predicts held-out choices better than standard prospect theory and noisy cognition benchmarks. The results imply that fitted risk preference parameters need not reveal primitive preferences. They may partly reflect the optimal structure of finite representation.

title: Who Is Buying New York City's Small Homes?
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Who Is Buying New York City's Small Homes?
detail.abstract:
A single narrative dominates U.S. housing policy on small homes: that corporate and institutional investors are buying up the stock and crowding out ordinary buyers. The headline statistics are built on a name-based buyer flag-any deed whose grantee contains LLC, Inc, Corp, or Trust is counted as an investor. We show this measurement convention systematically overstates corporate capture because it conflates family trusts with investor entities, and the bias grows over time as estate-planning and deedprotection trust use rises. We resolve this with a full decomposition of the New York City deed record: 2.26 million 1-3 family transactions from 1966 through 2025, in which every buyer is classified as an individual, a family trust (race-imputed from the named beneficiary), an institutional trust, or an investor entity. Buyer and seller race is imputed using STRATA, a name-and-geography model scored on each party's own mailing address-not the property's neighborhood demographics (Chalavadi, Leitch, and Pastor, 2025).
Three findings follow. First, the standard name-based flag produces a '≈45% corporate' share of NYC small-home purchases in 2025; decomposing it reveals 23.9% genuine investor capture and 21.1% family trusts — overwhelmingly families holding their own homes. Second, investor capture is not an accelerating takeover but a one-time structural step that began at the 2008 financial crisis and has plateaued at roughly 2.5× its pre-crisis baseline for a decade. Third, for Black homeowners, the channel pulling homes out of Black ownership is the investor/institutional buyer whose beneficial race is unobservable — the LLC-transparency gap — not white in-migration and not the trust surge, which is the same Black families. Net Black homeownership growth collapsed from +3,400 annually in 2008 to +90 in 2025. The policy implication is direct: beneficial-ownership disclosure is the binding constraint, and investor-share measures that conflate family trusts misdirect intervention.

title: Gross Flows and the Money-Creation Channel: Evidence from the United Kingdom

detail.title: Gross Flows and the Money-Creation Channel: Evidence from the United Kingdom
detail.abstract: Financial crises are commonly analysed through credit stocks and sectoral financial balances, both of which conceal the gross flows behind them. In the balance-sheetrecession literature, a rising private-sector surplus is often taken to indicate a desire to reduce net indebtedness, either by repaying debt or by accumulating money assets. This paper separates the relevant gross flows: new lending, repayment, and money-asset acquisition. It shows that a surplus cannot identify the process that produced it. New lending and repayment change deposits and debt by equal amounts and therefore cancel from the surplus by construction. The evidence must therefore come from the flows themselves. Using UK data, we find no evidence of either accelerated debt amortisation or money hoarding during the crisis years. New mortgage lending fell by 63.5 per cent. Scheduled repayments were essentially unchanged, while voluntary repayments fell by 31.9 per cent. The firm sector shows the same pattern. Net acquisition of money assets fell in both sectors and was negative for firms in the acute crisis year. The private-sector surpluses were real, but they arose neither from debt repayment nor from money hoarding. They reflected the collapse in private money creation through new lending, while deficit finance and quantitative easing sustained broad money.

title: Mortgage Lock-In and the Federal Reserve's Quantitative Tightening Shortfall

detail.title: Mortgage Lock-In and the Federal Reserve's Quantitative Tightening Shortfall
detail.abstract: U.S. agency mortgage-backed securities buy To-Be-Announced market liquidity with pool homogeneity built from standardized fixed-rate contracts whose par-payoff obligation, enforced through due-on-sale, locks households into below-market coupons when rates rise: secondary-market liquidity purchased at the price of household mobility. This paper measures that trade-off's cost to the Federal Reserve during Quantitative Tightening, when agency MBS runoff fell $764.7 billion short of the phased redemption caps over June 2022-November 2025. It cost less than the shortfall suggests. A loan-level survival framework built from Freddie Mac performance data recovers 91.3% of that shortfall on a benchmark-consistent accounting basis at the off-window calibration this paper headlines, 88.2-93.7% across that calibration's defensible range; at the in-sample calibration point on which the framework was assembled it recovers 97.9%. A null with the lock-in elasticity removed still recovers 85.7% at the headline calibration (88.7% in-sample), because scheduled amortization and baseline involuntary turnover undershoot a $35 billion monthly cap under any household response to rates. The Federal Reserve's own ex-ante projection anticipated the large majority of the realized shortfall. Measured against that projection rather than the never-binding cap, the lock-in channel accounts for between roughly a quarter and half of the genuine surprise, depending on a disclosed intra-2022 allocation choice: the settlement-aware allocation matching the realized settlement pattern gives the quarter, the pre-committed uniform-spread central allocation the half. The design identifies a bounded range for the elasticity's contribution, not a pinned magnitude, and it identifies levels only: no monthly-timing claim survives its own placebo tests, and the margin's sign is fixed by a rate configuration that leaves essentially the whole book out of the money for the whole window rather than by the estimated elasticity. Re-anchoring the involuntary-turnover floor that dominates the level outside the evaluation window and off the locked-in population puts that contribution at +5.6 percentage points over the mechanical null (+$42.6 billion), +4.3 to +6.8 points across the off-window floor's defensible range under the production hard-maximum floor form (+3.0 to +8.0 once the floor reads' cluster-bootstrap sampling error is propagated, and open below +4.3 on an age-standardized read); under the disclosed additive floor form the same off-window anchors return +11.2 points nearly floor-invariantly, so the form-conditional identified range is +3.9 to +13.1 points, of which +5.6 is the max-form member; the in-window production calibration returns +9.2 points, which I now report as an in-sample calibration point rather than the headline. The margin is positive at every floor and elasticity-band combination tested—a specification check the rate configuration cannot let fail, retained as such—and its magnitude is unchanged under a floor calibrated only on the window’s first nineteen months, an input-stability check rather than an outcome holdout. An agent-based model of the moving decision recovers 13.6% averaged across seeds, though a cross-design variant recalibrated on real loan covariates recovers 59.3% (76.3% reweighted to the book’s composition). The contrast cannot be cleanly attributed to modeling paradigm. The mobility cost is real. The institutional cash-flow cost is small, and its sign turns on the transplant’s anchor rather than on any sensitivity swept within an anchor: importing Denmark’s baseline mobility along with its payoff rule yields roughly −$100 billion, while a transplant changing only the payoff rule yields +$61 billion at the in-sample calibration point and +$28 billion at the off-window calibration the headline marginal uses. The latter’s positivity, and its survival of the refinancing sweep, follow from anchoring the Danish leg at the U.S. zero-gap hazard on a book that is out of the money almost everywhere; the informative quantity there is the magnitude, not the sign.
