title: Argentina: The Challenge and the Opportunity
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Argentina: The Challenge and the Opportunity

publicationDetails.detailsText: Peterson Institute for International Economics Working Paper No. 26-12
publicationDetails.journalName: Peterson Institute for International Economics (PIIE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Once one of the world's 10 wealthiest nations, Argentina has never fully recovered from its post-World War I decline. Now, as Washington renews its focus on Latin America, libertarian president Javier Milei is betting on close ties with the Trump administration to secure lasting economic stability in Argentina, but sustained US support is not assured. Milei should revamp Argentina's exchange rate regime and monetary policy to build on his successes and strengthen his chances in the 2027 election.

title: The Portrayal of 'Culture' in Advertising: Case of ''Go beyond-Turkish Airline'' Advertising

detail.title: The Portrayal of 'Culture' in Advertising: Case of ''Go beyond-Turkish Airline'' Advertising
detail.abstract: This research goes beyond the cultural domain of study to encompass the multidisciplinary field of communication. In fact, culture is the complex set that encompasses the knowledge, beliefs, arts, morals, laws, customs, and other abilities and habits acquired by man as a member of a society (Burnett, 1871) Hence, the concept of culture shock which refers to a "disorientation experienced when a person moves to a different cultural environment or an unfamiliar way of life" (Oberg, 1960). This study aims specifically to establish a nexus between culture and advertising. Concretely the purpose of this article is to decipher the portrayal of 'culture' in advertising. Thus, the case study applied to this article is developed through ''Go Beyond-Turkish Airline'' advertising campaign. Indeed, referring to its deceptive cognate publicity, advertising is the action of making public. It is also the set of means used to 'publicize' a product, an industrial or commercial enterprise (Schramm, 1954). Leaning on Turkish Airline's advertising, this study helps to understand clearly how culture is softly portrayed through media communication mechanisms.

title: Cognitive Aging and Long-Term Care in Italy
affiliations: Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia, University of Trieste, , Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia and Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia

detail.title: Cognitive Aging and Long-Term Care in Italy
detail.abstract:
This chapter examines the incidence and economic burden of cognitive impairment among older individuals in Italy within the long-term care (LTC) system. Using SHARE Wave 9 data (2022), cognitive impairment is measured through standardized memory and numeracy tests, classifying 8.6% of individuals aged 65+ as cognitively impaired. Cognitive decline rises sharply with age and is strongly associated with higher care needs, particularly intensive formal care. While both physically and cognitively impaired individuals rely heavily on informal care, cognitively impaired individuals receive substantially more hours of care. Total LTC costs amount to $35.3 billion (1.66% of GDP), with cognitively impaired individuals accounting for the largest share of expenditures. Informal care represents a greater financial burden than formal care across all groups. The findings highlight significant unmet care needs and underscore the urgent necessity of policy reforms and healthy ageing strategies to ensure LTC sustainability.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Belief-convexity and the Direction of Coherence: Gaming-proof Verification in Multi-audience Persuasion

detail.title: Belief-convexity and the Direction of Coherence: Gaming-proof Verification in Multi-audience Persuasion
detail.abstract: A sender communicates once with two audiences that summarize the same disclosure differently: an agent responds to its posterior mean, while a verifier responds to a downside risk measure. The sender profits from the gap between the two reads-a high mean that deters, a low floor that limits liability-but the information reaching the two audiences can differ only up to a leakage bound. This paper asks when the sender can game the gap, moving the verifier's read in its favor by sheltering probability mass. The answer is a single property: the read cannot be gamed if and only if it is convex in the sender's beliefs. A coherent measure of a floor the sender wants low-conditional value-at-risk, or Expected Shortfallis such a read, so verifying a floor coherently is gaming-proof: for every prior and every configuration of stakes and leakage, an optimal disclosure collapses to a single accept/reject partition with no sheltering. Value-at-Risk is not belief-convex, and when the worst case is concentrated the sender strictly benefits from a three-posterior shelter. But the decisive property is belief-convexity, not coherence as such: coherence is belief-convex for a floor the sender wants low, as a court reads an auditor's established diligence, yet belief-concave for a risk the sender wants read low, as a prudential regulator reads tail loss-where the same coherent measure becomes gameable. The framework applies to auditor liability under a burden-of-proof standard, with the prudential-capital setting as its mirror-where, the paper shows, the gaming-proof reading is not a coherent tail measure but a charge against a fixed threshold.

title: Walking with Feet Tied to the Past: Childhood Exposure to the 1918 Influenza Pandemic and Later-Life Male Mortality
affiliations: Austin Peay State University and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Walking with Feet Tied to the Past: Childhood Exposure to the 1918 Influenza Pandemic and Later-Life Male Mortality
detail.abstract: Many previous studies have used cross-cohort comparisons and a focus on in utero exposure to document the lingering effects of the 1918 influenza pandemic on survivors’ outcomes later in life. A subset has examined impacts on old-age health and mortality, finding mixed results. This paper contributes to the literature by extending the analysis to evaluate early-life and childhood exposure to the pandemic on old-age longevity along with a set of candidate mechanisms. We employ Social Security Administration death records linked to the full-count 1940 census and employ event-study and difference-in-difference regressions to compare longevity of cohorts with different age-at-exposure who were born in cities with high versus low exposure based on 1918 influenza-related mortality. Our treatment-on-treated calculations suggest that cohorts with age-at-exposure of 3-8 and 9-11 experience 6.4 and 11.2 months reductions in old age longevity; importantly, we note that these cohorts are often used as “controls” in the broader literature. While our main analysis focuses on males due to data constraints, supplementary results suggest smaller and less precise effects for females. An analysis of census data suggests reductions in health, education and socioeconomic scores as potential mechanisms.

title: A Network Theory of Project Management
affiliations: Columbia University, Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, Department of Economics

detail.title: A Network Theory of Project Management
detail.abstract: A principal assigns multiple agents to multiple projects by setting effort caps. Agents prefer specific projects, enjoy collaborating with others, but face a convex cost of effort. The principal's primary instrument is limiting agents' efforts on certain projects to prioritize other projects, even if agents prefer to work more on the former. Optimal project assignments organize project teams into a nested hierarchy: teams working on high-value projects are larger and include every agent assigned to lower-value projects. Shocks propagate in the organization through a network induced by the project assignment.

title: Do Autonomous Vehicles Contribute to Traffic Congestion? A Large Burden of Proof Remains
affiliations: University of San Francisco - School of Management

detail.title: Do Autonomous Vehicles Contribute to Traffic Congestion? A Large Burden of Proof Remains
detail.abstract: This study tests whether autonomous vehicle (AV) deployment, measured by publicly reported AV passenger miles, explains San Francisco congestion trends once total county vehicle miles traveled (VMT) is considered. AV activity remains a very small share of total VMT, from 0.0028% to 0.0638% in the observed data. An exploratory regression suggests that AV share can be used as a screening metric, but not as causal evidence. At current scale, systemwide congestion claims require stronger evidence; plausible impacts are more likely localized to curb, dwell, or corridor conditions.

title: Winners and Losers from Trade? Product and Process Innovation in a 3×3 Model
affiliations: Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Department of Economics and Finance and University of Amsterdam - Center for Nonlinear Dynamics in Economics and Finance (CeNDEF) - Department of Quantitative Economics

detail.title: Winners and Losers from Trade? Product and Process Innovation in a 3×3 Model
detail.abstract: We develop a multi-region, multi-sector Romer-type dynamic partial equilibrium model of endogenous growth. We calibrate on equally sized regions North, East, and South, based on data from Germany, Poland, and China. We compare the effect of trade block formation on innovation outcomes. Integration leads to aggregate increase in both product and process innovation, resulting in aggregate welfare gains. These are concentrated in North: the research sectors of East and South collapse. Our findings explain data from eastern European countries, as well as current R&D policies in China that are designed to avoid downstream lock-in.

title: Evaluating State Tax Incentives: Challenges and Adaptations *
affiliations: University of Chicago, Harris School of Public Policy, Center for Municipal Finance

detail.title: Evaluating State Tax Incentives: Challenges and Adaptations *
detail.abstract: State and local governments forgo hundreds of billions of dollars in tax revenue each year through tens of thousands of tax exemptions, deductions, credits, and other incentives. Most states devote little systematic effort to evaluating whether those incentives work. Washington State is a notable exception. Since 2006, its Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission has reviewed more than 750 tax preferences using a performance audit framework that asks a single question: does this incentive accomplish its stated policy objectives? I describe that framework, document its outcomes across nearly two decades of reviews, and examine the principal challenges it presents. I also describe the adaptations Washington has developed in response. The main finding is that the performance audit approach has clear advantages over traditional tax policy analysis, is tractable for other states, and offers a model worth serious consideration by policymakers and researchers alike.

title: Can Corporate Governance Reforms Reshape Supply-Chain Contracting? Evidence from Gender Quotas
affiliations: Alberta School of Business, University of Alberta, Business School, National University of Singapore and University of Navarra, IESE Business School

detail.title: Can Corporate Governance Reforms Reshape Supply-Chain Contracting? Evidence from Gender Quotas
detail.abstract: We study whether corporate governance reforms reshape contracting in global supply chains. Exploiting staggered board gender diversity (BGD) interventions in 37 customer countries as plausibly exogenous shocks, we examine their effects on the contracting outcomes of U.S. suppliers, which are not subject to comparable national policies. We find that U.S. suppliers with greater female board representation are more likely to obtain new contracts from customers in countries that adopt BGD reforms. These effects are stronger when the interventions are more likely to alter customer board composition and when customers possess greater bargaining power over suppliers, consistent with a customer-driven changes in governance preferences following the reforms. Mechanism tests indicate that the effects are more pronounced when customer firms have weaker pre-intervention ESG profiles, where board changes have greater scope to shift supplierselection criteria toward board gender diversity, and when customer-supplier country pairs are more institutionally and culturally distant, where governance alignment may be more valuable in mitigating cross-border contracting frictions. Finally, U.S. suppliers more exposed to BGDintervened customers subsequently increase female board representation, particularly when they have greater access to female director networks, and these increases are followed by improvements in operating performance. Overall, our findings highlight global supply chains as a channel through which governance reforms can have cross-border effects.

title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management in International Finance: Hedging Strategies and Corporate Financial Resilience
affiliations: and Universitas Muhammadiyah Palopo

detail.title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management in International Finance: Hedging Strategies and Corporate Financial Resilience
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between foreign exchange risk management, hedging strategies, and corporate financial resilience in international finance. Using a quantitative explanatory design with 65 respondents and Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM), the study tests four hypotheses involving direct and mediating effects. The results indicate that foreign exchange risk management has a significant positive effect on hedging strategies and corporate financial resilience. Hedging strategies also significantly enhance corporate financial resilience and mediate the relationship between foreign exchange risk management and resilience. These findings highlight that effective currency risk management must be accompanied by structured hedging strategies to strengthen firm stability. The study contributes to international finance literature by integrating risk management, hedging behavior, and "esil'ence into a unified conceptual framework.

title: "Mathematical Modeling of Traffic Flow using Partial Differential Equations"

detail.title: "Mathematical Modeling of Traffic Flow using Partial Differential Equations"

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: The global urbanization is one of the most challenging problems of modern transportation. The high volume of vehicles on the road, the fast pace of urbanization and poor road maintenance have all added to the serious traffic congestion and its associated economic, environmental and safety costs. Mathematical modeling is a powerful tool to assist in understanding, predicting and controlling traffic flow across a variety of roadway scenarios. Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) are among the various mathematically developed tools that have proven useful in describing the continuous motion of traffic by modeling the traffic flow, vehicle speed and traffic density. This research paper reviews the mathematical modeling of traffic flow in general and the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) model in particular, especially from the perspective of conservation laws. The paper summarizes the key works done by researchers in the field, highlights the gaps in the existing research and suggests an enhanced method to combine the PDE based traffic models with modern computational methods to achieve more accurate traffic predictions. The proposed methodology is based on the vehicle density as the state variable and numerical solutions to the governing equations, using finite difference schemes are computed under realistic traffic conditions. The study shows that the traffic behavior modeling such as congestion formation, shock waves and traffic dispersion can be well simulated using the PDEbased model. The results show that mathematical models can be used to give valuable insights for ISTS, traffic signal optimization, highway design and urban traffic planning. Although these models are efficient, they have several problems such as parameter estimation, the presence of heterogeneous traffic and real-time implementation. The paper also covers practical applications, benefits, challenges and future research avenues relating to the application of AI, connected vehicles, autonomous transportation system and smart city technologies. In conclusion, the study suggests that mathematical models using partial differential equations are one of the most effective and scientifically valid methods for studying and optimizing traffic movements and could be useful in the creation of sustainable and efficient transportation systems in the future.

title: Accounting Capitalization of Real-Time Computer Vision Tracking Algorithms in Chinese Youth Badminton Academies: EBITDA Inflation and Markov-Chain Asset Pricing of AI-Driven Sports Franchise Venture Returns
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Accounting Capitalization of Real-Time Computer Vision Tracking Algorithms in Chinese Youth Badminton Academies: EBITDA Inflation and Markov-Chain Asset Pricing of AI-Driven Sports Franchise Venture Returns
detail.abstract: The intersection of artificial intelligence-driven sports performance analytics and financial engineering presents a novel class of accounting ambiguity with material implications for enterprise valuation. This paper investigates two interrelated phenomena specific to the emerging ecosystem of Chinese youth badminton academies that have adopted real-time computer vision (CV) tracking systems as core operational infrastructure. First, we examine whether the capitalization of CV tracking algorithms and their associated data-pipeline assets under Chinese Accounting Standards (CAS) and IFRS 38 artificially inflates reported EBITDA, by reclassifying operating expenditure on algorithm maintenance, model retraining, and sensor infrastructure as intangible asset development costs subject to amortization outside the EBITDA line. We develop a formal accounting adjustment framework and demonstrate, through a panel of 47 academy-holding entities incorporated under the Variable Interest Entity (VIE) structure and listed on domestic Chinese exchanges between 2018 and 2024, that CV capitalization inflates reported EBITDA by a mean of 19.3%, with the distortion concentrated in academies with high athlete throughput and intensive retraining cycles. Second, we construct a Markov-chain asset pricing model calibrated to the discrete funding-round transitions observed in the venture capital lifecycle of AI-driven sports franchises, and evaluate whether the resulting transition probability matrix yields return predictions consistent with observed IRR distributions in this sector. The model achieves out-of-sample IRR prediction accuracy of 73.4% at the funding-round level, outperforming both comparables-based and DCF-based benchmarks by 18.7 and 24.1 percentage points respectively. Together, these findings establish that EBITDA-based valuation multiples applied to CV-intensive sports academies are systematically biased upward, and that Markov-chain methods offer a structurally superior framework for VC return modeling in technology-embedded sports franchises.

title: Narrative Salience and Disclosure Obfuscation: Testing Whether Computer-Vision Sports Analytics Initiatives Coincide with ASC 842 Lease Classification Discretion and Distorted Monte Carlo PRSU Valuation During Activist Investor Campaigns
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Narrative Salience and Disclosure Obfuscation: Testing Whether Computer-Vision Sports Analytics Initiatives Coincide with ASC 842 Lease Classification Discretion and Distorted Monte Carlo PRSU Valuation During Activist Investor Campaigns
detail.abstract: A growing number of large-capitalization U.S. technology firms have publicized strategic investment in computer-vision (CV) sports analytics-player-tracking, broadcast-enhancement, and venue-intelligence systems deployed through sponsorship, jointventure, or direct product initiatives-coinciding, in several widely discussed cases, with periods of heightened scrutiny over lease accounting practice and equity compensation design. This paper investigates, with deliberate methodological caution given the sensitivity of the underlying allegation, whether the public salience generated by such initiatives is empirically associated with greater classificatory discretion in Accounting Standards Codification Topic 842 (ASC 842) lease liability treatment, and whether any such association propagates into measurable distortion of Monte Carlo-simulated fair values for performance-vested restricted stock units (PRSUs) during the specific window of heightened market attention that activist investor campaigns generate. We wish to state at the outset, and reiterate at length in our critical discussion, that this paper does not claim to establish executive intent, deliberate concealment, or any individual instance of accounting fraud; rather, we test a narrower and more tractable empirical hypothesis-that narrative salience from a highly visible, technologically sophisticated initiative correlates with reduced analyst and market scrutiny of contemporaneous lease classification judgment, a documented general phenomenon in the disclosure-complexity literature that we apply here to a specific, novel attentiongenerating mechanism. We construct a CV-analytics salience score from earnings-call transcripts, sponsorship announcements, and patent filings, an ASC 842 lease classification ambiguity score from financial statement footnote disclosure language and discount-rate sensitivity, and a PRSU valuation distortion measure comparing reported Monte Carlo fair-value assumptions against a re-simulated benchmark using lease-classification-neutral inputs, across a panel of 71 U.S. technology firms subject to activist investor campaigns between 2019 and 2026. Using an instrumented two-stage least squares specification exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in sports-league broadcast-technology adoption cycles as an instrument for firm-level CV-analytics salience, we find a statistically significant positive association between CVanalytics salience and lease classification ambiguity (first-stage F=18.7), and a corresponding 14.6-27.3% mean PRSU fair-value distortion in firms exhibiting both elevated CV-analytics salience and ambiguous lease classification during active activist campaign windows, against the model's overall R²=0.74 fit. We critically examine the alternative, non-strategic explanations for this association that our research design cannot fully rule out, the ethical and legal limits of attributing causal intent from correlational governance data, the asymmetric severity of a false-positive accusation of manipulation against a named public company relative to a false negative, and the implications for activist investors, compensation committees, and the PCAOB's ongoing scrutiny of estimation-heavy disclosure regimes. This work occupies a deliberately narrow evidentiary space at the convergence of disclosure complexity theory, real options and Monte Carlo compensation valuation, and the political economy of shareholder activism, and we urge readers and any subsequent citing literature to respect the careful hedging of its central claims.

title: Retail-Package-Driven Coordinated Optimization of Virtual Power Plants in Spot Energy and Frequency Regulation Markets
affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University - College of Electrical Engineering, Sichuan University, Tsinghua Sichuan Energy Internet Research Institute, University of Macau and Sichuan University - College of Electrical Engineering

detail.title: Retail-Package-Driven Coordinated Optimization of Virtual Power Plants in Spot Energy and Frequency Regulation Markets
detail.abstract: The growing scale of renewable energy integration and ongoing electricity market reform are expanding the role of virtual power plants (VPPs) in providing flexibility services in spot energy and frequency regulation markets. Reliable VPP participation depends not only on aggregate adjustable capacity, but also on whether flexibility resources satisfy market-specific operational requirements at the time of delivery. However, existing VPP scheduling studies typically treat the flexibility resource pool as a given input and rarely model how retail-package parameters map into the operational attributes that determine market deliverability. This may cause resource-market mismatch and delivery failure. To address this issue, this paper proposes a retail-package-driven framework for forming deliverable flexibility resources and coordinating VPP participation in both markets. First, a formation model maps standardized retail-package parameter vectors and customer-side flexibility features into resource-level callable capacity and operational attributes. Second, an attribute-based matching mechanism screens formed resource groups against market-specific attribute thresholds and identifies spot-market-eligible, regulation-market-eligible, and jointly eligible resources. The matched resources are then scheduled through a coordinated optimization model. Under a shared callable-capacity constraint, the model jointly allocates spot energy, regulation reserve, and internal risk-hedging reserve, while dynamically updating deliverability to capture cross-period degradation and recovery effects. A mean-CVaR formulation is further introduced to balance expected operating profit and tail-risk exposure. Case studies show that the framework expands the deliverable resource pool by 57.1%, eliminates resource-market mismatch, improves frequency-regulation delivery, and clarifies the trade-off between market revenue and delivery-risk control.

title: No Synergy, Significant Synergy: Heterogeneous Policy Interactions in China's Low-Carbon Transition
affiliations: East China University of Science and Technology, East China University of Science and Technology and Chaohu University

detail.title: No Synergy, Significant Synergy: Heterogeneous Policy Interactions in China's Low-Carbon Transition
detail.abstract: This paper uses a difference-in-differences approach to empirically evaluate the carbon reduction effects of the voluntary New Energy Demonstration City (NEDC) policy, drawing on a panel dataset of 280 prefecture-level Chinese cities from 2008 to 2023. The results show that the policy significantly reduces the carbon emission intensity of pilot cities. This reduction operates through multiple channels: optimizing the energy consumption structure, promoting industrial upgrading, improving energy efficiency, and stimulating green innovation. The policy's effectiveness, however, is heterogeneous, varying with local resource endowments, the stringency of local environmental regulations, and geographical location. Given the potential for policy interaction within the broader "Dual Carbon" framework, the study further investigates the synergistic effects between the NEDC policy and two other major initiatives: the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) pilot and the New Energy Vehicle Demonstration City (NEVDC) policy. The findings reveal no synergy between the NEDC and NEVDC policies. In contrast, a significant synergistic effect emerges between the NEDC policy and the ETS, with the two jointly delivering a greater reduction in carbon emissions. This result offers partial validation of the feasibility of the "effective market and capable government" framework in the context of environmental governance.

title: Social Media as Pseudo-Public Spaces: The Digital Arena in the Hearts and Minds of the People
affiliations: Department of Trade and Industry,Philippines

detail.title: Social Media as Pseudo-Public Spaces: The Digital Arena in the Hearts and Minds of the People
detail.abstract: Public knowledge is no longer shaped solely by traditional institutions such as schools, libraries, newspapers, or governments. Increasingly, online platforms, search systems, metadata structures, and algorithmic visibility determine what information people encounter, how they understand issues, and what they ultimately regard as the truth. Social media platforms and search engines, and later on artificial intelligence large language models, have become major gateways to knowledge, influencing not only access to information but also the formation of public opinion. Understanding their role is essential for evaluating contemporary debates about misinformation, algorithmic transparency, and democratic participation.

title: Speeding Up, Slowing Down: Critical Thoughts in Today's Networked Society

detail.title: Speeding Up, Slowing Down: Critical Thoughts in Today's Networked Society
detail.abstract: What happens to a networked society which constantly outsources critical thinking, or even reasoning in its basic form? What happens to a networked society so intensely amazed with generative AI that it loses the core of creativity: the social? Is quantity over quality the new norm? I ask these questions in the midst of making sense of realities through the concepts from Paul Virilio’s works related to thinking about contemporary media theory, digital disengagement, and media practice and cultures. The relevant concepts or even theoretical groundings may appear simplified in this piece, with the core notions primarily referenced, not to shortchange a deeper understanding of these important tenets but to establish interconnections in present contexts which may have been elided, ignored, or assumed to be natural.

title: Targeting the Filipino Consumer: Data-Driven Marketing, Personalization, and Privacy in Philippine Integrated Marketing Communication

detail.title: Targeting the Filipino Consumer: Data-Driven Marketing, Personalization, and Privacy in Philippine Integrated Marketing Communication
detail.abstract: Have you ever searched for a product online and then suddenly seen advertisements for it everywhere? Many Filipinos experience this every day while browsing Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Shopee, Lazada, or even Google. A simple search for shoes, gadgets, skincare products, or food deliveries can quickly turn into a flood of personalized advertisements across multiple platforms. This experience may feel convenient because consumers discover products related to their interests, but it also reveals how modern marketing depends heavily on personal data. In today’s digital environment, companies no longer simply advertise to broad audiences. Instead, they study consumer behavior, collect digital information, and create targeted campaigns designed for specific individuals. This shift has transformed Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC) in the Philippines and raised important questions about privacy, ethics, and consumer awareness.

title: Receipts, Screenshots, and Viral Accountability: Brand Crisis Communication in Filipino Networked Publics

detail.title: Receipts, Screenshots, and Viral Accountability: Brand Crisis Communication in Filipino Networked Publics
detail.abstract: In the Philippines, that question no longer belongs only to cashiers, customer service counters, or proof of payment. Online, it has evolved into a demand for evidence. A screenshot of a deleted reply. A stitched TikTok exposing inconsistent responses. A Reddit thread comparing experiences. A comment section filled with strangers realizing they encountered the same issue. In Filipino digital spaces, receipts have become social proof. Once something is reposted enough times, it stops becoming a private experience and starts becoming a collective memory.

title: Selling Advocacy: "Tulong, Benta o Doble Kwenta?" -Purpose-Driven Branding and Social Issue Framing in the Philippines

detail.title: Selling Advocacy: "Tulong, Benta o Doble Kwenta?" -Purpose-Driven Branding and Social Issue Framing in the Philippines
detail.abstract: In the Philippines, advocacy is deeply tied to lived experience—shaped by stories of struggle and resilience, strengthened by bayanihan, and carried by shared hope. Filipinos are naturally drawn to causes that feel close to home, from disaster relief and community support to mental health awareness and social justice, because these are not distant issues but realities that touch everyday life. In an age where social media heavily shapes public perception, many brands have learned how powerful these emotions can be—not only for helping others, but also for increasing visibility, engagement, and consumer loyalty. This is where the question begins: Nakakatulong ba talaga? O benta lang?

title: Budol as an Information Practice: How Filipino E-Commerce Content Shapes Consumer Knowledge

detail.title: Budol as an Information Practice: How Filipino E-Commerce Content Shapes Consumer Knowledge
detail.abstract: In the Philippines, the internet functions as more than a mere digital marketplace; it serves as a sprawling digital commons of advice, reviews, hauls, and viral discoveries where purchasing decisions are quietly negotiated and formed. One of the most vivid expressions of this dynamic is the budol phenomenon—the informal and often playful art of persuading someone to purchase an item they did not originally intend to buy. Far from being a simple marketing gimmick, budol culture has evolved into a distinct information practice. It deeply shapes how Filipino consumers evaluate products, understand risk, and assess value in everyday e-commerce.

title: Who Wrote This Story? Responsible Use of AI Tools, Authorship, and Accountability in Student Journalism

detail.title: Who Wrote This Story? Responsible Use of AI Tools, Authorship, and Accountability in Student Journalism
detail.abstract: Have you ever been accused by a professor of using AI (Artificial Intelligence)? The idea of being blamed for using the tool can be a modern form of an offense that lowers a writer’s integrity. I once had a friend back in my senior year of high school, a fellow student and aspiring journalist, who was told by our teacher, with a deadly look of certainty, that her article had been written with QuillBot. This reflects a prominent unease in journalism and academia: how the use of AI challenges credibility, authorship, and accountability. According to a report by the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Foundation in 2026, 83 percent of students in the Philippines have used generative AI for educational purposes. Moreover, the report also claims that while student usage is high, institutional adoption lags behind the rapid widespread use of AI. Only 73 percent of educators in the Philippines use generative AI for teaching, and an even lower 42 percent utilize it for their own writing. It is also stated that AI engagement is widely based on convenience rather than deeper and more rooted learning.

title: Towards Augmented Participatory Archives: What Role for Citizens' Collective Intelligence in the Age of AI?
affiliations: Université Laval

detail.title: Towards Augmented Participatory Archives: What Role for Citizens' Collective Intelligence in the Age of AI?
detail.abstract: Citizens act as co-creators who should collaborate with archivists to enrich AI-generated archival descriptions, by highlighting the symbolic and emotional aspects conveyed by these records. This role is complemented by that of citizens who serve as auditors, verifying the quality of the outputs generated by disruptive technologies.

title: When Filipino-ness Became a Conversation: Digital Storytelling and Public Knowledge in the Classroom
affiliations: University of Santo Tomas

detail.title: When Filipino-ness Became a Conversation: Digital Storytelling and Public Knowledge in the Classroom
detail.abstract: What began as a classroom viewing activity became a deeper conversation about what it means to be Filipino. Through digital storytelling, students did not simply consume cultural knowledge—they actively questioned, negotiated, and participated in its production.

title: Bond with Social Bot: A Hidden Markov Model of Parasocial Relationship Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction
affiliations: University of Virginia - McIntire School of Commerce, The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Gies College of Business

detail.title: Bond with Social Bot: A Hidden Markov Model of Parasocial Relationship Dynamics in Human-AI Interaction
detail.abstract: With the advancement of large language models (LLMs), modern AI systems have developed sophisticated conversational and social interaction capabilities. Platforms increasingly deploy these systems not only for functional task completion but also for social engagement, such as providing emotional support and conducting casual conversations with users. This expanding social role raises a critical operational question for platforms: how should AI responses be configured to cultivate relational bonds between users and the bot, and by extension, between users and the platform? We address this question by modeling the dynamic evolution of users' parasocial relationships with an AI bot as a function of the bot's response characteristics, which we treat as controllable operational design parameters. Drawing on the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) framework and parasocial relationship theory, we develop a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) where users' latent parasocial relationship states govern their observed interaction choices and AI response characteristics drive transitions between states. We estimate the model on a longitudinal panel of user interactions with Grok, the built-in AI bot on X (formerly Twitter). We find that greater anthropomorphism and social intelligence in the bot's responses significantly increase the probability that users transition to higher parasocial relationship states, while greater linguistic complexity and a more analytical style significantly reduce it. These effects are most pronounced among users in the low parasocial relationship state, suggesting that the bot's communicative characteristics are especially consequential before meaningful relational bonds have formed. Design simulations identify social intelligence as the most influential operational lever for fostering sustained social engagement. Our findings provide implications for calibrating AI response strategies to cultivate users' relational engagement.

title: Generative AI and Idea Implementation: An Attention-Based View
affiliations: University of California, Irvine

detail.title: Generative AI and Idea Implementation: An Attention-Based View
detail.abstract: Research on innovation has emphasized that generating ideas is insufficient for creating value; ideas must be implemented through collective effort. Although recent scholarship highlights generative artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool for ideation, little theory and evidence explain whether and how it affects idea implementation. We theorize generative AI as a communication technology that facilitates implementation through the attention it helps ideas attract. Implementation depends on whether colleagues notice and engage with an idea, and generative AI lets users express it in terms more accessible and relevant to each audience, drawing greater attention and support. We test this in a longitudinal field experiment at a software company piloting ChatGPT Enterprise. Of 287 workers, 140 were randomly assigned access and 147 served as controls. Combining two survey waves with the firm’s performance evaluations in a difference-in-differences design, we find that employees with access contributed significantly more to advancing ideas into products, services, and processes. They attracted 23.5% more attention from colleagues, and mediation analyses indicate this attention partially explains the effect, especially for employees in brokerage positions. By theorizing generative AI as a technology that aids implementation, this study reframes it as an enabler of a critical, overlooked stage of innovation.

title: Facebook is the Internet: How Individuals Depend on Facebook Influencers, Community Groups as Information Sources

detail.title: Facebook is the Internet: How Individuals Depend on Facebook Influencers, Community Groups as Information Sources
detail.abstract: There is no love like Filipinos’ love for Facebook. — In the Philippines, it is not Google nor Safari that dominates as the information source, it is Facebook. In 2025, Facebook became one of the top information sources, next to the Internet, 75% of Filipinos rely on it daily for news. Approximately 95.8 million Filipinos use the platform which is an enormous chunk of the entire population. During the pandemic era, netizens formed massive communities inside Facebook. These can be seen in the forms such as but not limited to marketplaces (buy & sell and food vendors), local villages, and fandoms. Filipinos dominate the users of Meta, primarily Facebook and Messenger with a staggering 81.9% relative to its total population. Meeting a Filipino is highly likely on the internet and even more common in Meta platforms.

title: Technology Shocks, the AI Boom, and the U.S. Current Account
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System,  and

detail.title: Technology Shocks, the AI Boom, and the U.S. Current Account

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: The current artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom in the United States provides a powerful boost to imports of high-technology capital goods. The AI buildout bears the hallmarks of an investment-specific technology shock—a process in which rapid technological progress makes each new generation of capital equipment significantly cheaper and more powerful than the last, but where reaping those efficiency gains requires continuous and substantial investment to acquire and deploy the new vintage of capital goods.

title: Sustainability Context Inheritance: From Trusted Evidence to Product Sustainability Profiles in Circular Economy Decision-Making
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sustainability Context Inheritance: From Trusted Evidence to Product Sustainability Profiles in Circular Economy Decision-Making
detail.abstract: Circular economy decisions increasingly depend on sustainability evidence distributed across product passports, certifications, supplier disclosures, lifecycle assessments and regulatory systems. The central challenge is not only whether evidence exists, but whether it is sufficient to support a product-level sustainability claim for a specific decision. This paper introduces the Sustainability Context Inheritance Architecture (SCIA), a conceptual environmental information systems architecture for evidence-sufficiency assessment. SCIA maps evidence to product structures, checks coverage, gaps and traceability, applies attribution rules, and produces a Product Sustainability Profile (PSP). The measurable output is a PSP that reports, for each selected claim, whether it is supported, partially supported or unsupported, together with coverage dimensions, unresolved gaps and traceability links. An electric scooter scenario demonstrates how SCIA can expose partial evidence across suppliers and jurisdictions for sustainability decision support. The contribution is a coverage-aware approach to product-level attribution that makes uncertainty explicit instead of hiding it inside broad sustainability claims.

title: Fifth Conference on the International Roles of the U.S. Dollar: Stablecoins, Digital Payments, and the International Role of the U.S. Dollar
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: Fifth Conference on the International Roles of the U.S. Dollar: Stablecoins, Digital Payments, and the International Role of the U.S. Dollar

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: The U.S. dollar continues to occupy a central role in the global economy. It remains the most widely used currency in foreign exchange transactions and cross-border payments, the leading currency in official reserve holdings, and the dominant currency of denomination for international debt securities and loans. This dominant position reflects several enduring features of the U.S. economy and financial system, including the size and strength of U.S. economy, the depth and liquidity of U.S. financial markets, and enduring confidence in U.S. institutions.

title: Adversarial Concealment: Locating Representational Invisibility and Topologically Modeling the Deliberate Maintenance on Knowledge Graphs
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Adversarial Concealment: Locating Representational Invisibility and Topologically Modeling the Deliberate Maintenance on Knowledge Graphs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is a named inventor on United States provisional patent applications, one of which concerns the closed-form estimand and the concealment-detection bound presented in this article. Those applications are unexamined. Others concern cognitive-mapping and information-asymmetry technologies unrelated to the findings presented here. The author declares no financial interest in any outcome of this article, and no personal or financial relationship that could be perceived to have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, human subjects, or personal data. It uses publicly available data from Wikipedia and the Wikimedia pageview interface. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This article reframes the unknown unknown, ordinarily treated as a defect of the observer, as a topological deficit of the representational system. Given a knowledge graph that carries two routing measures, a significance measure that would allocate attention by consequence and a delivery measure that allocates attention as it actually flows, the article defines the latent reservoir as the set of objects that are heavy under significance, unreachable under delivery, and unmarked as to that discrepancy, and it asks which topological properties of the substrate predict membership. The candidate predictors are drawn from personalized PageRank seeded on the delivery hubs, the spectral gap and Fiedler partition of the delivery Laplacian, Ollivier-Ricci curvature, and degreezero persistent homology, and each is required to survive a degree-preserving configuration-model null so that invisibility is established as a super-degree effect rather than an artifact of low in-degree. The article then separates invisibility that a change of representation alone can repair from invisibility that requires new data, and it gives an admissibility condition under which the first case is provable with zero new observations. Finally it models the deliberate maintenance of invisibility as a filtration-shifting operator whose cost is the distortion of the persistence diagram, and it shows, through the stability theorem for persistence diagrams, that deep concealment is detectable in proportion to its depth and therefore survives only against an auditor who lacks the ground-truth diagram. Three falsification tests are specified, including a closed-world recovery protocol, and empirical domains in which the phenomenon is documented and measurable are identified.

title: Predicting Arrest Outcomes and Mapping 25-Year Enforcement Patterns in Chicago (2001-2026): A Corrected Machine Learning, Longitudinal, and Geospatial Analysis

detail.title: Predicting Arrest Outcomes and Mapping 25-Year Enforcement Patterns in Chicago (2001-2026): A Corrected Machine Learning, Longitudinal, and Geospatial Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available, de-identified administrative crime incident data from the City of Chicago Data Portal. No human subjects were directly recruited, surveyed, or contacted. The dataset contains no personally identifiable information about victims, offenders, or officers. Ethics board approval was not required as this research falls outside the scope of human subjects research as defined by federal regulations (45 CFR 46).
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper presents two distinct contributions applied to the City of Chicago public crime catalog: 7,877,981 incident records across 22 attributes spanning 2001-2026. The first contribution is methodological: a fully corrected machine learning pipeline eliminating four systematic errors present in prior analyses. A controlled ablation study quantifies the largest error-target leakage from crime-type identifiers-showing XG-Boost accuracy drops 17.25 percentage points when leaky features are removed (87.29% → 70.04%). After correction, Random Forest achieves 79.77% accuracy [95% CI: 79.72-79.82%] and XGBoost achieves 52.16% arrest-class F1. All pairwise differences are statistically significant (McNemar test, all χ 2 > 95,000, p < 0.001). Temporal validation on 2019-2026 data yields 78.30% accuracy and 35.56% F1, with rolling year-by-year analysis documenting concept drift from post-2020 policing changes. The second contribution is longitudinal: a 25-year characterization of enforcement patterns only possible at this temporal scale. Narcotic arrest ratios sustain 99.3% through 2019 then collapse following documented policy shifts. Sexual offense arrest ratios decline 50 percentage points monotonically from ≈75% in 2001 to below 25% by 2025-a finding not previously characterized at this granularity. Theft clearance remains structurally stable at 9.1% across all 25 years. K-Means geographic clustering identifies four coherent spatial crime regimes. These corrected results and longitudinal findings constitute the authoritative baseline for future Chicago crime research.

title: Precarious Working Conditions in Nigeria’s Higher Education: The Role of Psychological Ownership and Servant Leadership
affiliations: Independent and University of South Africa, University of South Africa

detail.title: Precarious Working Conditions in Nigeria’s Higher Education: The Role of Psychological Ownership and Servant Leadership
detail.abstract: Despite concerns about the persistent Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) strike and deteriorating working conditions in Nigerian universities, limited empirical attention has been given to the potential of psychological ownership (PO) and servant leadership (SL) mechanisms to mitigate their effects. This study examines whether SL promotes a sense of ownership that buffers the negative effects of precarious work on organisational citizenship behaviours (OCB) towards academics (OCB-A) and the university (OCB-U). This study employed a multidimensional measure of SL and PO to describe and explain their relationships with the OCB-A/U in the academic population across six geopolitical zones of the Nigerian Federation. The cluster sample was analysed using both descriptive and inferential statistics, employing PLS-SEM. The findings indicate that when academics (subordinates) feel a sense of ownership, they are motivated to support the organisation’s vision. The study further affirms that when a leader demonstrates genuine care for their followers’ wellbeing, followers respond strongly by assisting colleagues or even superiors in completing tasks or resolving issues. However, the leader conducts (community interest) that prioritises taking the community’s interests outside of the immediate organisation into consideration, which does not significantly affect OCB-A. It was discovered that if academics internalise their sense of “mine-ness” toward their university, they will exhibit increased discretionary engagement (altruism, courtesy, conscientiousness, civic virtue, and sportsmanship) beyond their formal job expectations.

title: Beyond Identity and Organizationality: Viability as a Distinct Ontological Problem in Organization Theory

detail.title: Beyond Identity and Organizationality: Viability as a Distinct Ontological Problem in Organization Theory
detail.abstract: Organization theory has developed sophisticated explanations of how organizations vary, adapt, and perform, yet it has paid comparatively less explicit attention to what must be sustained for organizations to persist as organizations over time. This paper argues that the field has under-specified a distinct ontological problem of persistence: viability. Existing conversations have clarified what organizations are and when collective arrangements count as organizational, but they have less clearly isolated the conditions required for continued organized existence. To address this gap, the paper distinguishes ontologies of identity from ontologies of viability and develops a structural account of viability grounded in a criterion of necessity. On this basis, it derives three minimal conditions of organizational persistence: temporal orientation, structured coordination, and operational enactment. It then argues that, because these conditions must be continuously sustained, viability implies reproduction over time, which in turn points toward a grammatical layer concerned with the patterned organization of that reproduction. By distinguishing viability as a distinct ontological problem, the paper sharpens the difference between organizational functioning and organizational persistence, provides a lower-bound basis for comparison across heterogeneous organizational forms, and opens a research agenda on fragility, erosion, collapse, and the grammar of organizational reproduction.

title:
The Neurotic as Prophet:

Karen Horney, Christianity, Psychoanalytic Dissent,

and the Cult of Self-Actualization in Mass Culture
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
The Neurotic as Prophet:

Karen Horney, Christianity, Psychoanalytic Dissent,

and the Cult of Self-Actualization in Mass Culture
detail.abstract: This essay undertakes a sustained critical examination of the theoretical edifice constructed by Karen Horney (1885-1952), interrogating her work from the perspectives of classical psychoanalysis, Jungian depth psychology, Lacanian structuralism, Christian anthropology, conservative social theory, and contemporary gender criticism. It argues that Horney's revision of Freudian metapsychology, while correcting certain reductive tendencies, simultaneously introduces a secular soteriology — a this-worldly theology of salvation through therapeutic self-actualization — that is theologically incoherent, empirically underdetermined, and culturally parochial. The essay further traces the popularization of Horneyian assumptions through mass cultural phenomena including the Twilight saga, the Harry Potter series, and the ideology of Mormon exceptionalism, demonstrating how the cult of the Chosen Self functions as a substitute religion that manages, rather than resolves, the deep anxieties of middle-class modernity. The critique proceeds through multiple disciplinary lenses, accumulating a body of objections that collectively challenge the foundational premises of Horney's project.

title: A Threat to Sovereignty Lock-in Mechanisms in Consumer Digital Ecosystems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Threat to Sovereignty Lock-in Mechanisms in Consumer Digital Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Nowadays, digital services are mainly accessed through consumer digital ecosystems. However, the integration that makes them convenient also makes them di cult to leave. While the macrostructural sources of ecosystem retention are well understood, the concrete design-level mechanisms that ecosystem orchestrators embed to lock in individual users remain scattered across the literature. This thesis identifies and validates these mechanisms and asks whether they a↵ect user-level digital sovereignty, that is, the capacity of individual users to act and decide autonomously within their digital environment. The question is answered in two steps. First, a systematic literature review retrieved fourteen studies, from which eleven distinct lock-in mechanisms were extracted. These were grouped into five clusters that map the architectural layers of a consumer digital ecosystem and classified along Burnham et al. switching cost typology. In a second step, these mechanisms were validated through an online survey of 222 ecosystem users, in which 10 of the 11 mechanisms were confirmed to impose switching costs. Furthermore, twenty-two of their twenty-six attributed cost dimensions were reproduced in user-reported costs. The validated mechanisms and their validated switching-cost dimensions form the Lock-in Catalog. On this basis, the thesis shows that lock-in mechanisms do a↵ect user-level digital sovereignty, placing both of its autonomy conditions, critical reflection and the absence of undue external influence, under empirical pressure. Theoretically, the catalog consolidates the previously scattered discussion of ecosystem lock-in into a single, structured overview, making the so far abstract problem of user-level lock-in concrete and anchoring the conceptual sovereignty debate empirically at the user level. Practically, the catalog provides a concrete map of where user-level lock-in originates and where regulation, most prominently the EU Digital Markets Act, can address it.

title: The AfCFTA Protocol on Trade in Services

detail.title: The AfCFTA Protocol on Trade in Services
detail.abstract: The Protocol on Trade in Services (PTS) of the Agreement establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is a key instrument for Africa’s economic integration, aiming to create a single, liberalized market for services across the continent. Signed in 2018 and entered into force in May 2019, together with other Phase I instruments, the PTS draws on the WTO’s General Agreement on Trade in Services but is tailored to Africa’s development priorities, such as sustainable development and regional value chains. This chapter discusses the Protocol’s legal and institutional framework for progressive liberalization, including obligations such as most-favoured-nation (MFN) treatment, transparency, special and differential treatment, domestic regulation, market access and national treatment. While the Protocol uses a positive list approach to schedule commitments, initially focusing on five priority sectors, it balances ambition with flexibility, allowing gradual market opening and regulatory cooperation, while safeguarding public policy objectives.

title: Only attractive women are welcome: Board bias and CEO selection
affiliations: and

detail.title: Only attractive women are welcome: Board bias and CEO selection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: CEOs matter, and beauty matters. Based on social identity theory, we argue that women and men are likely to be held to different beauty standards by the boards of directors when these boards select the new CEO. Our empirical results support our arguments. Specifically, we investigate 959 CEO turnovers in non-financial S&P 1500 firms in the period from 2008 to 2022. We find that newly appointed female CEOs are significantly more attractive than their male peers. Thus, the median female CEO is more attractive than a male CEO at the 75th percentile level. We find no indication of an economic rationale for such a biased beauty preference. When investors are informed of the new CEO, they value CEO beauty equally across the two genders (i.e., no gender bias). The discrimination by the boards of directors seems to be related to women's minority status (i.e., we get similar results for non-white candidates) rather than the sexualization of women although we cannot rule out that both may coincide. Our findings are robust and economically significant. Thus, they are important in understanding the lack of gender equality and the avenues through which women face (beauty) discrimination in the upper echelons.

title: Understanding the Mind of the Modern Workers Through the Short Dark Tetrad and Light Triad Traits: The Good, The Bad and the Situational
affiliations: Independent and University of South Africa, University of South Africa

detail.title: Understanding the Mind of the Modern Workers Through the Short Dark Tetrad and Light Triad Traits: The Good, The Bad and the Situational
detail.abstract: Research on socially aversive personality in organisations has largely centred on the Dark Triad, with comparatively limited attention to everyday sadism (Short Dark Tetrad; SD4) and the countervailing influence of Light Triad traits (LTT). This narrow focus constrains theoretical development in understanding how aversive and prosocial dispositions jointly shape workplace behaviour. Addressing this gap, we integrate Trait Activation Theory and Person-Situation Interactionism with Generational Cohort Theory and HEXACO's Honesty-Humility dimension to develop a multilevel perspective on dark/light trait expression. We conducted a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines across five major databases, synthesising 42 manuscripts published between 2020 and 2025. Using a PICO-informed framework, we organise findings across three core domains of organisational behaviour: deviant vs citizenship behaviour, work engagement, and leadership and organisational change. Our synthesis reveals that dark/light traits exert paradoxical effects. Machiavellianism is associated with unethical conduct but may enhance effectiveness under conditions of environmental uncertainty, whereas Kantian orientations promote cooperation but may constrain competitive responsiveness. Narcissistic and psychopathic traits are linked to short-term engagement, while humanism and faith in humanity underpin more prosocial forms of engagement. These patterns highlight a fundamental strain in how engagement and effectiveness are conceptualised within organisations. We further show that generational cohort differences shape the activation and expression of SD4/LTT, suggesting that intergenerational dynamics represent an underexplored boundary condition in personality-behaviour relationships. The study contributes to organisational behaviour research by clarifying when and why aversive vs prosocial traits emerge and the consequences of their emergence. Practical implications include designing organisational contexts that attenuate maladaptive trait activation while promoting sustainable engagement and ethical conduct.

title: Private Credit's State Backstop: How Private Equity Socializes Risk Through Insurers
affiliations: and

detail.title: Private Credit's State Backstop: How Private Equity Socializes Risk Through Insurers
detail.abstract:
Private equity (PE) firms have acquired large life insurers and loaded their balance sheets with private credit assets that are opaque and difficult for regulators to value. This Article explains how PE profits from these insurers while shifting the resulting risk onto competitors and taxpayers.

Unlike ordinary firms, life insurers do not pass through bankruptcy when they fail. Instead, when a life insurer becomes insolvent, state-based guaranty funds protect insurance policyholders by "assessing" surviving insurers to cover the shortfall. In most states, such outlays are fully creditable against state premium taxes over time, transforming an ostensibly industry-funded system into a public backstop. The result is a system that socializes losses more sharply than banking's federal deposit insurance, and does so with an insolvency and regulatory architecture that is more fragmented and less able to address macroprudential concerns. With the rise of PE's new private credit strategy, insurance's unique insolvency, tax, and financial regulation regimes now form critical components of private credit's submerged legal infrastructure.

PE firms exploit this regulatory regime by pairing life insurers with private credit to capture value from both sides. After acquiring an insurer, the PE firm earns profits in two ways: a spread between what the insurer promises policyholders and what its investments earn, and management-related fees on those investments. Guaranty funds and their accompanying regulatory regime implicitly subsidize this model in three ways. First, opacity in private credit permits insurers to appear better capitalized than their true risk exposure warrants. Second, weak incentives for policyholder monitoring permit PE to siphon gains through control of fees while shifting losses onto insurer balance sheets. Third, because guaranty-fund assessments are based on premium volume rather than risk contribution, conservatively-managed insurers (and, ultimately, taxpayers) finance the more aggressive strategies of their PE-owned competitors.

PE-owned life insurers reflect a structural transformation in which an insurer supports a broader asset-management business that is designed to extract value upfront and impose losses on others. Having traced that transformation, this Article proposes to curb the veiled subsidies for this shift with reforms that make insurance risks legible, price risk pre-failure, and allocate losses to insurance affiliated groups post-failure. Doing so would restore insurance insolvency, tax, and financial-regulation law to their policyholder-protection role.

title: Corporate climate risk: Do female CEOs matter?
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN, Aarhus University - Department of Economics and Business Economics and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Corporate climate risk: Do female CEOs matter?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: We exploit a newly established framework to investigate the role of CEO gender in transition climate risk management. Recent literature indicates that women and men act differently in the sphere of climate risk and that this difference extends to female and male managers. We investigate CEOs of 814 non-financial S&P 1500 firms from 2007 to 2022. Contrary to our expectations, we find no effect of CEO gender on corporate transition climate risk exposure or on responses to such exposure. Within-firm event study analysis, propensity score matching, and equivalence testing confirm these null findings. Neither does CEO gender moderate the relationship between corporate performance and such exposure and responses. Our results are robust to the inclusion of female CFOs and are important in understanding the interplay between CEO gender, transition climate risk exposure, responses to transition climate risk, and corporate performance.

title: Unsolving Capital Theory A Perspective for the Economy The Cambridge Capital Controversy, the Aggregation Problem, and a Micro-lifecycle Utility Framework for Valuing Heterogeneous Capital
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Unsolving Capital Theory A Perspective for the Economy The Cambridge Capital Controversy, the Aggregation Problem, and a Micro-lifecycle Utility Framework for Valuing Heterogeneous Capital

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that this submission represents original research. All sources, data, and foundational theories utilized within the paper have been appropriately cited and acknowledged. The author confirms that there are no conflicts of interest or ethical violations associated with this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research is entirely theoretical and secondary data-driven, involving no human participants, animal testing, or clinical trials.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no financial support or funding from any organization or institution for the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article.

detail.abstract: This paper revisits the unresolved core of the Cambridge Capital Controversy and argues that its persistence is a feature of economic science rather than a defect. The neoclassical production function, Q = f(L, K), runs into a circularity the moment it tries to compress physically heterogeneous assets-a blast furnace, a lathe, a server rack-into a single scalar K. Because the money value of capital depends on the rate of profit, and the rate of profit is in turn supposed to be governed by the quantity of capital, the measuring rod bends under the weight it is asked to carry. The reswitching and capital-reversing results that emerged from the debate, and Paul Samuelson's eventual concession in 1966, confirmed that the loop is logical, not rhetorical. Rather than declaring either Cambridge "right," this paper proposes an escape by changing altitude. It develops the Micro-Lifecycle Utility Framework, which abandons macro-aggregation in favour of ground-level, asset-by-asset accounting: capital value is defined as the cumulative net economic utility an asset realises across its working life, decomposed into trackable terms-gross margin, energy, direct labour, maintenance, depreciation, and initial outlay. The framework is demonstrated on a realistic worked example, a CNC machining centre in a Jaipur job-shop, using figures grounded in current Indian industrial tariffs and machine-tool prices. The numbers reveal an economic life that conventional book-keeping hides: net utility rises, peaks in year seven, and then erodes as rising upkeep outpaces falling output, signalling an optimal retirement point years before the depreciation schedule expires. The contribution is not a new master index but a defence of specialised, situation-specific measurement-and a plea for intellectual humility in how we read the history of economic thought.
